cold_email.subject: Interest in Seasonal Educator / Citadel Outlets — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Seasonal Educator / Citadel Outlets opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Center for Health and Wellbeing Patient Service Representative — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear University of Vermont Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Center for Health and Wellbeing Patient Service Representative opportunity with University of Vermont at University of Vermont.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Student Content Creator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear MyEdSpace Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Student Content Creator opportunity with MyEdSpace at MyEdSpace.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in CDL Admissions Representative (65437) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear International Education Corporation Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the CDL Admissions Representative (65437) opportunity with International Education Corporation at International Education Corporation.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in School Administrative Assistant — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear FullBloom Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the School Administrative Assistant opportunity with FullBloom at FullBloom.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Assistant/Analyst — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear City of New York Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Assistant/Analyst opportunity with City of New York at City of New York.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.body:
Dear VIP (Vermont Information Processing) Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Assistant Pre-School Teacher opportunity with VIP (Vermont Information Processing) at VIP (Vermont Information Processing).

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,

cold_email.subject: Interest in Admissions Officer — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear South College Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Admissions Officer opportunity with South College at South College.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Data Analyst I or II - Statistics and Data Science research support opportunity with NORC at the University of Chicago at NORC at the University of Chicago.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. Dear Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Laboratory Logistics -Sample Splitter (2nd Shift) - Eurofins Environment Testing - 2 Shifts Available opportunity with Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) at Eurofins Environment Testing (USA).

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Resident Services Coordinator I - 801 Alma, Studio 819, and Brookwood, Mountain View/Palo Alto/San Jose CA Hay — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Eden Housing, Inc. Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Resident Services Coordinator I - 801 Alma, Studio 819, and Brookwood, Mountain View/Palo Alto/San Jose CA Hay opportunity with Eden Housing, Inc. at Eden Housing, Inc..

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Lab Tech 1 Allegheny County 15205 (M-F 7:30am-4:30pm or 8:00am-5pm) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear ABB OPTICAL GROUP Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Lab Tech 1 Allegheny County 15205 (M-F 7:30am-4:30pm or 8:00am-5pm) opportunity with ABB OPTICAL GROUP at ABB OPTICAL GROUP.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Support Coach — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Opportunity Partners Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Support Coach opportunity with Opportunity Partners at Opportunity Partners.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Software Developer II - ServiceNow
jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Position Summary At BMS, digital innovation and Information Technology are central to our vision of transforming patients’ lives through science. To accelerate our ability to serve patients around the world, we must unleash the power of technology. We are committed to being at the forefront of transforming the way medicine is made and delivered by harnessing the power of computer and data science, artificial intelligence, and other technologies to promote scientific discovery, faster decision making, and enhanced patient care. The ServiceNow Developer is responsible for the design, development, and implementation of complex ServiceNow solutions. This includes working with business stakeholders to understand their needs and develop solutions that meet those needs. The ServiceNow Developer will also be responsible for maintaining and enhancing existing ServiceNow applications, as well as troubleshooting and resolving any issues that arise. If you want an exciting and rewarding career that is meaningful, consider joining our diverse team! Key Responsibilities Design, develop and implement complex ServiceNow solutions. Develop Service Catalog items, workflows, and service request processes. Work with business stakeholders to understand their needs and develop solutions that meet those needs. Maintain and enhance existing ServiceNow applications. Troubleshoot and resolve ServiceNow issues using problem-solving skills. Stay up to date on the latest ServiceNow features and functionality. Contribute to the development and implementation of ServiceNow platform, including core functionalities, modules, and best practices. Communicating and collaborating with cross-functional teams, to identify and document business processes that can be automated using ServiceNow. Working with a team of IT Operations engineers to integrate ServiceNow with other IT systems, such as monitoring and ticketing systems. Participate in daily stand-up meetings to provide progress updates and address any blockers. Working with a user experience mindset to develop and deploy solutions for customers. Participating in Agile planning ceremonies to help define and prioritize ServiceNow work for the upcoming sprint. Developing and testing ServiceNow solutions in accordance with the Agile methodology. Deploying and supporting ServiceNow solutions in a production environment. Experience in designing and implementing Service Catalog items, workflows, and service request processes. Must be self-directed with proven ability to make mature decisions supported by thorough data and process analysis. Monitoring ServiceNow performance and troubleshooting any issues that arise. Sharing knowledge and best practices with other team members through code reviews, pair programming, and training sessions. Mentor and train junior ServiceNow developers. Qualifications & Experience Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, related field, or equivalent work experience 3-5+ years of experience in ServiceNow development and implementation Experience with the following ServiceNow modules: o IT Service Management (ITSM) o IT Operations Management (ITOM) o IT Asset Management (ITAM) o Service Portal Experience with ServiceNow Flow Designer and Service Catalog Experience with Agile development methodologies Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills Strong communication and teamwork skills Experience with ServiceNow integrations Experience with ServiceNow reporting and analytics ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA), Certified Application Developer (CAD) or Certified Implementation Specialist (CIS) certification is a plus We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. How We Work Where you work matters – because collaboration, innovation and patient impact happen in many settings. Our roles are structured across four work models: site-essential, site-by-design, field-based and remote-by-design. The model assigned to this role is based on its core responsibilities. Learn more at https://careers.bms.com/ways-of-working. Supporting People with Disabilities BMS is dedicated to ensuring that people with disabilities can excel through a transparent recruitment process, reasonable workplace accommodations/adjustments and ongoing support in their roles. Applicants can request a reasonable workplace accommodation/adjustment prior to accepting a job offer. If you require reasonable accommodations/adjustments in completing this application, or in any part of the recruitment process, direct your inquiries to adastaffingsupport@bms.com . Visit careers.bms.com/eeo-accessibility to access our complete Equal Employment Opportunity statement. cold_email.subject: Interest in Software Developer II - ServiceNow — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Bristol Myers Squibb Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Software Developer II - ServiceNow opportunity with Bristol Myers Squibb at Bristol Myers Squibb.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Staff HRIS Analyst
jobs.description: What if the work you did every day could impact the lives of people you know? Or all of humanity? At Illumina, we are expanding access to genomic technology to realize health equity for billions of people around the world. Our efforts enable life-changing discoveries that are transforming human health through the early detection and diagnosis of diseases and new treatment options for patients. Working at Illumina means being part of something bigger than yourself. Every person, in every role, has the opportunity to make a difference. Surrounded by extraordinary people, inspiring leaders, and world changing projects, you will do more and become more than you ever thought possible. Position Summary: Illumina is seeking an experienced Staff Analyst, People Technology to support global HR technology programs. This role reports to the Associate Director, People Technology and serves as a senior functional owner for Workday Time Tracking, Absence, Benefits, and payroll-related integrations. Required Skills: Workday configuration: hands-on configuration and support for Time Tracking, Absence, Benefits, related business processes, validations, calculations, approvals, work schedules, eligibility, accruals, balances, enrollment events, plan rules, and life events. Payroll and benefits integrations: define functional requirements, data mappings, monitoring, reconciliation, exception handling, controls, and test coverage for payroll and benefit-provider interfaces. HR and payroll domain knowledge: understand time and absence calculations, payroll processing dependencies, benefit eligibility, enrollment events, and downstream processing controls. Reporting and analytics: build reports and dashboards for payroll readiness, interface monitoring, balance validation, benefit reconciliation, and operational decisions. Testing and releases: plan Workday releases and lead system, integration, regression, parallel, end-to-end, and user acceptance testing for HRIS changes. Security and data controls: protect the accuracy, confidentiality, security, and auditability of employee and payroll-related data across global systems. Automation and AI judgment: identify responsible automation or AI use cases with human review, privacy, access, accuracy, and audit controls. Key Responsibilities: Serve as the senior functional owner for Workday Time Tracking, Absence, Benefits, and payroll-related integrations, including roadmap and enhancement priorities. Lead end-to-end solution design across time capture and approval, absence eligibility and accruals, benefit enrollment and life events, and payroll data flows. Diagnose complex system, interface, security, and data issues with Payroll, Benefits, technical teams, and external vendors within required processing timelines. Lead global HR technology initiatives from scope, requirements, dependencies, schedule, risk, communications, and change planning through stabilization. Create clear procedures, runbooks, training, user guidance, requirements, testing materials, control documentation, and status reporting. Coach analysts and project team members on functional design, operational readiness, controls, and support practices. Required Qualifications: Typically requires a minimum of 8 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 6 years and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with 3 years of experience; or equivalent experience. Substantial hands-on Workday configuration and support experience across Time Tracking, Absence, Benefits, and payroll-related integrations in a complex organization. Experience defining data mappings, reconciliation methods, exception handling, and test coverage for HR, payroll, and benefits interfaces. Experience gathering requirements, analyzing business processes, and recommending practical system or process solutions. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, organizational, written, and verbal communication skills, with close attention to data quality and payroll-impacting deadlines. Ability to work effectively with technical and nontechnical stakeholders at multiple levels. Preferred Qualifications: Experience supporting global or multi-country time, absence, benefits, and payroll integration requirements. Experience developing Workday Extend applications and workflows. Experience with Workday reporting, security, integration tools, dashboards, and operational analytics. Experience applying AI, machine learning, robotic process automation, or workflow automation to HR technology operations within defined privacy and human-review controls. Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including formulas, pivot tables, and charts. Experience working with Agile, Scrum, or related delivery practices. Successful Candidate Profile: Applies systems thinking and HR business knowledge to turn complex requirements into practical, maintainable solutions. Balances detail orientation with a strong understanding of payroll deadlines, downstream impacts, and control requirements. Builds trusted partnerships across HR, Payroll, Finance, Technology, Audit, and external vendors without relying on formal authority. Communicates system and data risks, tradeoffs, recommendations, and required decisions clearly. Works independently, adjusts priorities, and handles sensitive data, access, AI, and automation with sound judgment and discretion. Preferred Educational Background: Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, Human Resources, or a related field. The estimated base salary range for the Staff HRIS Analyst role based in the United States of America is: $118,200 - $177,200. Should the level or location of the role change during the hiring process, the applicable base pay range may be updated accordingly. cold_email.subject: Interest in Staff HRIS Analyst — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Illumina Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Staff HRIS Analyst opportunity with Illumina at Illumina.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Data Center Design Manager
jobs.description: About the Team OpenAI's Compute organization builds and operates the infrastructure that powers frontier AI training and inference. Our data center engineering teams develop the technical standards and infrastructure required to deploy compute at unprecedented scale across both self-built and partner-operated environments. We work across civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, construction, and infrastructure delivery to develop data center designs that are reliable, scalable, and optimized for speed. About the Role We are seeking a Data Center Design Manager to coordinate the design and delivery of infrastructure for large-scale AI deployments. You will bring engineering disciplines and external design partners together to translate infrastructure requirements into coordinated, buildable design packages. You will manage design milestones, resolve cross-discipline interfaces, and keep technical decisions aligned with project requirements. Working with engineering, construction, commissioning, operations, and hardware teams, you will help preserve design intent from early planning through construction and turnover. The focus is design execution, technical coordination, and clear ownership of design decisions. Key Responsibilities - Manage design scope, deliverables, milestones, and dependencies from concept development through detailed design and construction support. - Coordinate civil, structural, architectural, mechanical, electrical, controls, and physical network interfaces across data center buildings and campuses. - Translate owner and hardware requirements into coordinated design criteria, working with discipline leads to resolve gaps and competing requirements. - Lead multidisciplinary design reviews; track comments, decisions, technical risks, and actions through resolution before design release. - Evaluate design changes with engineering and delivery partners, making impacts on reliability, safety, cost, schedule, and maintainability clear. - Coordinate external architects, engineering consultants, developers, and equipment suppliers to maintain design quality and meet agreed deliverables. - Partner with construction and commissioning teams on constructability, sequencing, RFIs, submittals, field issues, and design changes. - Maintain design documentation and handoff requirements, and incorporate field and operational lessons into reusable standards and reference designs. Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in engineering, architecture, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience. - Experience managing multidisciplinary design for data centers, mission-critical facilities, or comparable complex infrastructure. - Technical understanding of data center infrastructure and the interfaces among power, cooling, controls, structures, and physical networks. - Experience taking coordinated design packages from early planning through detailed design and construction support. - Experience coordinating external design consultants, engineering specialists, and construction partners. - Ability to read technical drawings and specifications, identify interface gaps, and work with discipline experts to resolve them. - Strong written and verbal communication, disciplined issue tracking, and sound judgment when balancing technical requirements with delivery constraints. Preferred Skills - Experience with hyperscale data centers, high-density AI or HPC infrastructure, or other rapidly evolving mission-critical environments. - Familiarity with liquid cooling, high-density power distribution, and the integration of changing compute hardware requirements into facility designs. - Experience managing design reviews, quality checks, and technical change control across concurrent projects. - Experience with modular or prefabricated infrastructure and design approaches that improve constructability and deployment speed. - Familiarity with BIM, model coordination, clash detection, and engineering document-control tools. - Experience supporting commissioning readiness, as-built documentation, and handoff to operations. - Experience adapting reference designs and engineering standards to site-specific constraints across a portfolio. - Professional engineering or architecture licensure, or relevant design and project management credentials. jobs.title: Event Operations Manager, Speaker Programs
jobs.description: Who We Are Strategic Event Services brings together strategy, operational excellence, technology, and cross-functional expertise to deliver high-quality experiences across congresses, speaker programs, and advisory boards. Our team works closely with Field, Marketing, Medical, Compliance, Legal, technology teams, speakers, and vendors. The Event Operations Manager reports to the Head of Strategic Event Services The role provides essential operational, compliance, financial, and administrative support, enabling smooth, compliant execution across a high volume of programs each year. We are looking for an Event Operations Manager who can provide end-to-end operational excellence while helping Strategic Event Services strengthen and continuously improve how speaker programs are delivered. The Opportunity The Event Operations Manager, Speaker Programs is the internal operational owner for assigned speaker bureaus and programs, from bureau setup through program closeout. You will support HCP programs (in-person, virtual), Patient programs, and HCP and Patient product theaters, most organized into brand bureaus that run on a calendar-year cycle. Our speaker program vendor manages day-to-day logistics and execution. You will direct that vendor, keep every program inside the compliance guardrails, and own the approval, financial, and documentation work that stays in-house. Responsibilities: Oversee Vendor Execution: Direct the day-to-day work of our speaker program vendor across logistics, registration, attendee management, and speaker coordination. Set clear expectations, monitor performance against SLAs and KPIs, and resolve or escalate gaps. Manage Bureau and Program Operations: Coordinate annual bureau setup and close, program intake, timelines, and readiness. Adapt requirements to each program type, including Patient program needs such as patient speaker training, privacy, and adverse event reporting. Operationalize Compliance: Partner with Compliance and Legal to confirm speaker contracting, fair market value, and training are complete before programs proceed, and that attendee, venue, meal, and state-specific rules are met. Manage Materials and Approvals: Route speaker decks, invitations, and program materials through Commercial and Medical review. Track re-approvals and expirations so only current approved materials are in use. Manage Financial Operations: Support budgets, statements of work, purchase orders, invoices, accruals, and reconciliation. Validate speaker honoraria and HCP spend for Open Payments (Sunshine Act) and state transparency reporting. About the role Enterprise is central to Anthropic's mission. The organizations that could benefit most from Claude often have the most demanding needs, with rigorous requirements around end-user experience, procurement, security, and permissions. We believe earning their trust is essential to ensuring AI benefits the world broadly. We're looking for a Staff+ Full Stack Engineer for our Enterprise pillar—the team that makes Claude enterprise-ready at scale. When a Fortune 500 company rolls out Claude to 100,000 employees, the admin, governance, and management experiences you build are what their IT leaders, security teams, and end users touch every day. This is a high-agency role where the product questions are as open as the architecture ones: you'll help decide what these products are, not just how they're built, and you'll see your work land with real teams at the world's largest enterprises. What you'll do Own technical design and delivery for enterprise-facing products end-to-end across the stack—from admin consoles and governance surfaces to the APIs and data models behind them Partner with product, design, and go-to-market to turn enterprise customer workflows into shipped product, not just execute against a spec Set technical direction and standards for your team: architecture, code quality, and how the team builds Work directly with enterprise customers, admins, and sales during key conversations, translating what you learn into engineering priorities Build the primitives that let the world's largest organizations deploy, govern, and get value from Claude at scale Mentor other engineers and raise the technical bar across the team, working with influence rather than authority You may be a good fit if you Have 8+ years of software engineering experience, ideally with 2+ years at a Staff or equivalent technical leadership level Have led the design and delivery of complex customer-facing products across the full stack Have built enterprise SaaS products and understand what IT admins, security reviewers, and procurement teams need to say yes Are comfortable working directly with enterprise customers and translating what you learn into technical decisions Have built products from 0 to 1 in fast-moving environments, and can set technical direction with limited precedent to lean on Drive cross-team alignment to ship impactful work, with influence over authority Strong candidates may also have Experience with enterprise identity, permissions, and administration surfaces (SSO/SCIM, RBAC, audit, usage and spend visibility) Experience building AI products and turning model capabilities into applications people actually use Experience as startup founders or early-stage employees The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $405,000 — $485,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. We ensure optimal performance of global application hosting and network services that power Pfizer's business processes. We strive to revolutionize service dependability by applying advanced analytics to drive predictive detection, identifying potential issues with our services and intervening before they disrupt our business. We place data at the heart of what we do and apply a relentless focus on continuous improvement to enable Pfizer's business processes and patient outcomes. We are seeking an AI Ops SRE Platform Engineer to build and own the platform behind our AI-driven operations and to act as technical coordinator for a small AI Operations pod within Hosting SRE Operations, based in Greece. This role leads the design and delivery of our agent-assisted incident pipeline - from intake classification and enrichment, through read-only investigation, to guarded remediation approved by a human. The successful candidate combines hands-on engineering of AI agents and automation with strong operations judgement, and will convert classic infrastructure operations across Server, Storage, Data Protection, Database, Middleware and HCI into reliable, measurable AI-driven operations. Role Responsibilities Accountable for the technical direction and coordination of the Greece AI Ops pod, aligning the team's work by influence rather than line authority, and acting as the senior technical decision-maker and escalation point when incidents or design choices exceed the pod's normal thresholds. Own the end-to-end design and delivery of the Agentic Ticket pipeline, from intake (classification, enrichment, prioritisation, routing) through cross-system investigation and root-cause drafting, accountable for its reliability, safety and readiness for production use. Own the capability contract that governs the agent runbooks, the integration allow-list, and read-versus-change scope per system, defined jointly with Platform and Cloud Engineering on a default-deny basis, exercising judgment over what the agent may safely be permitted to do. Set the standards for how connectors and remediation playbooks are built across the operational toolchain (e.g. ServiceNow, Dynatrace, Aria, AIQUM, Rubrik) with execution through SSM and Ansible, ensuring every automated action carries rollback and audit and meets the pod's safety bar. Hold the pipeline to explicit accuracy and reliability targets, validated against our own estate rather than vendor benchmarks, and judge when performance is trustworthy enough to move an action from human-approved to automatic. Embed SRE and automation-first ways of working across the pod, and hold accountability for continuous improvement and measurable toil reduction across the Hosting domains. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in a technical field or equivalent practical experience. 4 years+ in infrastructure operations, SRE or platform engineering, including a technical leadership or lead-engineer role. Demonstrated delivery of production AI-agent or automation systems (for example Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, LangGraph or equivalent), including tool and connector integration via MCP or similar. Strong programming and automation skills (Python plus one or more of Bash, PowerShell), CI/CD and coding best practices, and IaC / configuration management (Ansible, Terraform). Working knowledge of at least two Hosting domains (Server/OS, Storage, Data Protection, Database, Middleware or HCI) sufficient to judge remediation safety. jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As an Applied AI Engineer on the Startups team at Anthropic, you will be a trusted technical advisor to the top AI-native life sciences and biotech startups as they grow from early product to scale. Some of these companies build products on Claude that they sell to the rest of the industry, and others do the science themselves and want Claude woven into how their own research runs, and this role works with both. You'll lead deep technical engagements, partnering directly with startup engineering and scientific teams to help them build their products on Claude and run their own research with it, advising on implementation and agent design as they build what is newly possible with AI in the life sciences. You will bridge the gap between what Claude can do and what the life sciences need, working alongside some of the strongest teams in the field on problems that matter and pushing the boundaries of AI in science as you go. Working closely with Applied AI Architects, Account Executives, and Anthropic's Product, Engineering, and Research teams, you'll help startups build at the edge of what is possible with Claude. You'll leverage your AI engineering expertise and your scientific domain knowledge to develop custom evaluation frameworks, design scalable architectures, and create the technical resources that enable life sciences startups to succeed with Claude. Responsibilities Serve as a deep technical advisor to high-potential life sciences and biotech startups, whether Claude sits inside the product they sell or inside the way they make discoveries, working alongside them to build innovative use cases that push the boundaries of AI in scientific research and development Work hands-on with startup engineering teams and their scientists through pair programming and architecture reviews that accelerate their development, and understand their scientific workflows end to end so that your guidance fits into real research pipelines Develop prototypes and technical documentation, including evaluation suites, scientifically grounded benchmarks, AI engineering techniques, and architecture diagrams, that enable startups to build, operate, and scale with Claude Create reference implementations and sample code that many companies can adopt without starting from scratch, such as example MCP servers for domain-specific data sources like genomics platforms, literature databases, and experimental repositories, along with agent skills for common scientific workflows Collaborate closely with Applied AI Architects to maintain context and continuity across customer engagements Identify patterns across engagements, including what is hard about deploying AI in the life sciences such as heterogeneous data, auditability requirements, and the gap between a working prototype and a system that scientists trust, and contribute insights back to Product, Engineering, Research, and the broader Applied AI team, including feedback on the model capabilities and product features that would most accelerate discovery work Create technical content for startup audiences including documentation, tutorials, and sample code Represent Anthropic across the life sciences startup ecosystem and foster community engagement through hackathons, webinars, technical office hours, in-person founder events, and research show and tells Travel to customer sites for workshops, implementation guidance, and relationship building You may be a good fit if you have Deep experience in the life sciences or biotech, gained through research or industry work in areas such as genomics, drug discovery, molecular design, lab automation, or clinical development, along with strong opinions of your own about how to bridge the gap between what AI can do today and what the life sciences need 4+ years of technical experience as a software engineer, ML or research engineer, computational biologist, research scientist, or technical founder, with either production experience building LLM-powered applications, including prompting, context engineering, agent architectures, evaluation frameworks, and deployment at scale, or a track record of successfully applying AI to real scientific work in the lab or in research Experience with startups or high-growth companies and a love of working with founders and small teams that move quickly Strong technical communication skills, with the ability to translate complex AI concepts into architectural decisions and actionable implementation plans for both engineering and scientific audiences and to run technical workshops, hackathons, or developer-focused events A collaborative approach to working across teams, the ability to context-switch across scientific domains and use cases, and a passion for making powerful technology safe and beneficial The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $280,000 — $320,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. In this role, you will take connected devices from ambiguous user or business needs through system architecture, rapid prototyping, board design, firmware implementation, bring-up, field deployment, and production transition. The ideal candidate has a passion for building and shipping reliable hardware at scale and thrives in an environment that demands technical depth and high-quality execution across multiple concurrent programs. This is a build-heavy role on a small, senior team. Key Responsibilities Translate user and business needs into an integrated electrical and firmware architecture. Design compute-based, mixed-signal boards incorporating processors, power systems, sensors, wireless connectivity, displays, and other peripherals. Develop embedded firmware, selecting bare metal, FreeRTOS, embedded Linux, or Android based on product needs. Lead board bring-up, validation, and troubleshooting using lab tools (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, spectrum analyzers, network analyzers, etc.). Prototype with new sensors and run experiments to determine whether useful, reliable signals can be extracted. jobs.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Fraud Investigator (Customer Protection Team) is responsible for handling inbound customer calls for customers with an active fraud alert and account restriction. The team investigates fraud alerts, determining fraud or no fraud utilizing tools and investigative skills, and helping identify emerging fraud trends through data analysis. The team works directly with the customer via phone to gather additional information to help make a fraud determination on their account. This role is based in our Lake Mary, Florida or Denver, CO office(s), with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. Hours may vary from Monday through Friday between the hours of 7am to 9pm ET. . At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Conduct in-depth and timely investigations on accounts flagged for fraud, across a range of payment vehicles including ACH, Debit Card, Cryptocurrency and Wire Transfers Handling inbound phone calls from users with fraud restrictions and taking those fraud cases to the finish line by applying investigative techniques according to the internal procedures and policies Using critical thinking and pattern detection to discover proactive ways to identify emerging fraud Documenting the rationale and determination for each alert and referring to other teams where necessary Gathering key information from the customer regarding their account as well as applicable documentation. Communicating with customers next steps and setting expectations. What you bring 2+ years experience in fraud investigations including in-depth knowledge of various fraud activities such as Account Takeovers, Identity Theft, Money Mule, and Money Movement Fraud, among others; or, equivalent experience adjacent to fraud investigations. Proactively identify problems and come up with solutions (ability to think outside-the-box) Ability to operate in a fast paced environment Good written and verbal communication, analytical skills, and strong attention to detail Strong interpersonal skills, experience working with cross-functional teams such as product, engineering, legal, compliance, vendor partners, or financial crimes Passionate about mentoring and working with junior fraud investigators and agents to help guide and explore career Ability to work closely with customers to address concerns related to fraud while maintaining a high level of customer service Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) certification not required but a plus What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds. Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + benefits. Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to one of 3 compensation zones. For other locations not listed, compensation can be discussed with your recruiter during the interview process. Base Pay Range: Zone 1 (Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY; Bellevue, WA; Washington, DC) $31 — $37 USD Zone 2 (Denver, CO; Westlake, TX; Chicago, IL) $28 — $33 USD Zone 3 (Lake Mary, FL; Clearwater, FL; Gainesville, FL) $27 — $32 USD Click here to learn more about our Total Rewards, which vary by region and entity. If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application. AI Usage Disclosure: Robinhood uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of our recruiting process. These tools enhance the efficiency and consistency of our hiring process; however, all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams. Robinhood provides equal opportunity for all applicants, offers reasonable accommodations upon request, and complies with applicable equal employment and privacy laws. Inclusion is built into how we hire and work—welcoming different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences so everyone can do their best. Please review the Privacy Policy for your country of application.

jobs.title: Workplace Coordinator
jobs.description: WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS At Meter, we’re rebuilding networking from the ground up (hardware, software, and operations) so that enterprises can finally have networks that are fast, secure, reliable, and evolve without friction. Workplace Operations plays a critical role in bringing that mission to life by creating an environment where our people can do their best work every day. Workplace Coordinators are the first point of contact for visitors, setting the tone for their overall experience. They greet guests, assist with check-ins, and make sure everyone feels acknowledged and supported upon arrival. This role is also a key connection point between all Meter office locations — coordinating shared systems, supplies, and standards so every Meter, no matter their zip code, has what they need to do great work. This is a fully in-office role, based in our San Francisco office, serving as a consistent on-site presence for employees and guests. WHAT YOUR DAY WILL LOOK LIKE You'll spend much of your day at reception, as the first point of contact for guests, employees, prospects, and customers. Your warm, attentive presence sets the tone for everyone who enters the office. Day to day, you will: - Greet and check in guests, employees, and vendors - Accept, sort, and route all incoming packages and mail - Maintain a consistent inventory of supplies and snacks across all offices, on a set cadence - Own the ordering process end to end — from tracking stock to placing and reconciling orders - Coordinate with other office locations to keep standards and systems consistent company-wide WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE At three months, you know every SF Meter. You are aware of patterns and habits of Meters, guests, and vendors. You accept all packages and mail and manage their final destination. You’ve implemented an ordering system for all Meter offices. At six months, the function runs independently. You're anticipating problems, not reacting to them. People trust your judgment without needing to pressure-test your work. At one year, you've raised the bar on how the Workplace Coordinator works. You're improving the function, not just maintaining it. You’ve learned to triage, troubleshoot, and solve a wide array of workplace issues. Employees come to you to solve problems and you are looking to increase your scope at Meter. WHO YOU ARE You embody our culture of kindness, ambition, optimism, and paranoia, and take pride in creating environments where people feel welcomed and supported. The people you'll work with are genuinely kind and care deeply about doing great work. It's a supportive team that wants you to succeed, and expects the same ambition from you in return. Additionally, you have good taste. You notice when something is off, you know what great looks like, and you care enough to fix it. Beyond that: - You synthesize information and come with a recommendation, not just a summary of what happened - You carry context forward, prior decisions, established patterns, vendor history, without needing to be reminded - You follow through on straightforward next steps without someone checking in - You communicate clearly, in person and in writing, and people always know where things stand LEARN MORE ABOUT HOW WE OPERATE AND SOME OF OUR WORK - What is Meter? https://www.meter.com/what-is-meter - Meter: the internet utility https://www.notboring.co/p/meter-the-internet-utility by Packy McCormick - How we operate https://www.meter.com/careers#how-we-operate - Vertical integration in practice https://www.meter.com/blog/vertical-integration-in-practice WHY METER? The internet runs the world. Every email you send, purchase you make, video call you join—it’s all packets flowing through networks. But those networks haven’t changed for decades. They’re brittle, complex, and surprisingly hard to set up in an enterprise space. We started Meter to build better networks. We had to build everything from the ground-up: designing and building our own enterprise hardware, intuitive software, and streamlined operations to deliver great outcomes for our customers. Today, we build and deploy these networks at scale. Ambitious companies and enduring institutions like Bridgewater, Lyft, Reddit, rely on Meter to keep their thousands of employees and locations online and productive. Our bet with Meter is simple: we will all use the internet more than we do today. We believe we have the definitive networking stack in place to enable business to do so as seamlessly and reliably as any modern utility. We’re committed to building a diverse, inclusive team and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply. If you’re a California resident, you can learn more about how we handle applicant data here https://www.meter.com/careers/job-applicant-privacy. COMPENSATION - The estimated pay range for this role is $24.00-$30.00 per hour. - Additionally, this role is eligible to participate in Meter's equity plan

Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do. Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career. Associate IS Bus Sys Analyst What you will do Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. We are seeking a Senior Associate Business Analyst to partner with Operations stakeholders, Product Managers, Data Scientists, and Engineers to identify, define, and deliver Generative AI solutions that improve operational efficiency, decision-making, and user experiences. Gather, analyze, document, and validate business, functional, data, and reporting requirements. Facilitate stakeholder discussions, workshops, and requirements for gathering sessions. Create intuitive visualizations that communicate business performance, trends, and operational insights. Develop executive dashboards, operational reports, and analytical solutions for different stakeholder groups. Perform data analysis to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and actionable business insights. Ensure dashboard accuracy through data validation, reconciliation, and quality checks. Publish, maintain, monitor, and support dashboards in enterprise environments. Optimize dashboard performance, usability, accessibility, and adoption. Data and Technology Collaboration Work with data engineers, developers, architects, and technical teams to understand source systems, data structures, and integration needs. Support data mapping, validation, reconciliation, and root-cause analysis across multiple data sources. Assist in defining business rules, calculations, transformations, and reporting datasets. Create and maintain requirements, dashboard documentation, data definitions, user guides. Deliver dashboard demonstrations and solution walkthroughs to business and technical stakeholders. Stay current with business intelligence, analytics, visualization, and AI-enabled reporting capabilities. Basic Qualifications Bachelor's degree in information systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Business Administration, Data Analytics, or related fields. 3-5 years of experience in Business Analysis, Business Intelligence, Reporting and Analytics, Data Analysis, or a related role. Experience building KPI dashboards, executive scorecards, operational reports, and analytical visualizations. Strong SQL skills for data extraction, analysis, validation, and reporting. Expected to support RunOps for multiple Applications with knowledge on SaaS and COTS applications. Experience gathering, documenting, validating, and managing business and reporting requirements. Ability to translate business needs into effective data, dashboard, and analytics solutions. Experience creating user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows, data requirements, and functional specifications. Experience with relational databases, large datasets, data modeling concepts, data quality, and reconciliation. Experience publishing, maintaining, and supporting dashboards in enterprise environments. Experience supporting UAT, defect management, business validation, and release activities. Experience working in Agile or Scrum delivery teams and using Jira, Confluence, Azure DevOps, or similar tools. Strong stakeholder management, analytical, problem-solving, communication, and presentation skills. Ability to work effectively with global, virtual, and cross-functional teams. Good-to-Have Skills Experience in life sciences, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, healthcare, EHSS, manufacturing, or another regulated industry. Experience supporting Environmental, Health and Safety, Sustainability, Quality, Compliance, Operations, or Corporate functions. Experience with cloud-based data and analytics platforms such as Azure, AWS, Databricks, or Snowflake. Understanding data warehousing, ETL/ELT processes, APIs, integrations, and enterprise reporting architectures. Familiarity with Python or another analytics-related programming language. Exposure AI-assisted analytics, reporting, or business productivity tools. Experience supporting enterprise-scale reporting solutions and globally distributed business teams. Experience with Generative AI products and solutions Understanding of LLMs, copilots, chatbots, and AI assistants Prompt engineering concepts Soft Skills Strong analytical and critical thinking abilities. Excellent communication, facilitation, and stakeholder engagement skills. Ability to simplify complex data and technical concepts for business audiences. High degree of ownership, accountability, initiative, and attention to detail. Collaborative mindset with a focus on shared outcomes and business value. cold_email.subject: Interest in Associate IS Business Analyst — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate IS Business Analyst opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern, Frontend
jobs.description: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. Explore our Engineering Blog https://builders.ramp.com & Emerging Talent https://builders.ramp.com/emerging-talent Blog to learn more about how we build at Ramp and what it’s like to start your career here. ABOUT THE ROLE Ramp is, at its core, an engineering company. We’re looking for frontend and full-stack engineering interns who are excited to build intuitive, high-quality products that solve complex problems for our customers. Our ideal candidate has strong JavaScript fundamentals, an eye for great user experiences, and enjoys turning customer needs into thoughtful engineering solutions.
